title: This Dyslexia-Friendly Speed-Reading Tool Has Existed for Over a Decade.
snippet: This Dyslexia-Friendly Speed-Reading Tool Has Existed for Over a Decade. And Your Website Still Doesn’t Have It. A Tool That’s Been Hiding in Plain Sight There’s a piece of…
contentHtml:
This Dyslexia-Friendly Speed-Reading Tool Has Existed for Over a Decade. And Your Website Still Doesn’t Have It.

A Tool That’s Been Hiding in Plain Sight

There’s a piece of technology that’s been sitting around for over ten years. It’s backed by real science. It’s free, open-source, and any developer could add it to a website in an afternoon. And almost nobody uses it.

It’s called RSVP, which stands for Rapid Serial Visual Presentation. Don’t let the fancy name fool you. The idea is dead simple: instead of making your eyes scan across a line of text, the words come to you, one at a time, flashing in the same spot on the screen.

For most people, that sounds like a neat party trick for reading novels faster. But for the roughly 1 in 5 people in this country who deal with dyslexia, that “party trick” can be the difference between being able to read your website and giving up and leaving, according to estimates from groups tracking dyslexia prevalence in the U.S.

And here’s the part that should bother you as a business owner: this isn’t some experimental lab technology. It already works. It’s already free. Nobody’s building it into your website, your phone, or your browser. That’s not a technology problem anymore. It’s a “nobody bothered” problem.

How It Actually Works (No Tech Degree Needed)

Picture reading a sentence on a page. Your eyes don’t glide smoothly across the words like a video camera. They jump. Word to word, sometimes back up to re-read something, over and over, dozens of times per sentence. Those little jumps are called saccades, and they take up a surprising chunk of your reading time.

Frank Waldman, who built one of the first popular versions of this technology, put it simply in a 2014 NPR interview: roughly 80% of the time you spend reading normally isn’t spent understanding words. It’s spent physically moving your eyes around to find the next one. Stop the eyes from having to hunt, and your brain gets to spend almost all its time doing the one job that actually matters, which is understanding what it just read.

That’s the whole trick. The words show up exactly where your eye is already looking. No hunting. No scanning. Your brain just catches them as they come.

What the Research Actually Says (Including the Bad News)

Now, to be fair to you, this isn’t some miracle cure with zero downsides. A well-known 2015 study published in Computers in Human Behavior tested this technology on regular readers and found two real problems: it slightly hurt comprehension for some readers, and reading this way for a long stretch can tire your eyes out faster, partly because you blink a lot less while doing it.

So if you’re a totally average reader who has no trouble with normal text, this tool might not be your best option. Fair enough.

But here’s where it gets interesting. The exact same thing researchers flagged as a downside for typical readers (forcing your eyes to stop wandering and lock onto one spot) is precisely what makes this tool a lifeline for people whose eyes don’t cooperate the normal way in the first place.

People with dyslexia tend to have a much harder time controlling where their eyes land. They re-read more, lose their place more, and burn far more mental energy just managing eye movement before they’ve even started processing a word. Take that burden away completely, and the entire experience of reading changes.

It’s not just dyslexia, either. A 2025 clinical study on people with Friedreich’s ataxia, a disease that disrupts eye control, found this kind of word-by-word reading boosted their reading speed from about 164 words per minute up to roughly 233 words per minute. That’s nearly a 40% jump, simply because the technology routes around the broken part entirely. The eyes don’t have to behave. The brain still gets the words.

There’s even research on young adults with ADHD showing this same word-streaming approach can improve their reading comprehension, not just their speed.

This is the heart of good accessibility design. It’s not about making the fast thing faster for people who are already fine. It’s about giving an alternate path to people whose normal path is blocked.

Why This Should Actually Matter to You as a Business Owner

Here’s where this stops being a cool science story and starts being a real business issue.

First, the obvious one: customers. If 1 in 5 people struggle with reading conventional text, that’s a massive slice of your potential customer base quietly bouncing off your website, your menu, your service descriptions, or your blog, simply because reading a wall of text is exhausting for them. You’re not losing them because your content is bad. You’re losing them because the format doesn’t work for their brain.

Second, and this one should really get your attention: lawsuits. Website accessibility lawsuits aren’t some rare legal exotic anymore. In 2025 alone, businesses faced over 8,600 federal ADA lawsuits tied to digital accessibility, and there’s no small-business exemption written into the law. Most of these lawsuits target companies nowhere near Fortune 500 size. If your site isn’t built with accessibility in mind, you’re already exposed, whether you knew it or not.

Third, think about the competitive angle. Almost none of your competitors are offering anything like this. A simple “Read Mode” button that streams your blog post, your FAQ page, or your product descriptions word by word would make your business one of the only ones in your space actually solving this problem instead of ignoring it. That’s a cheap, easy way to stand out, and it happens to be the right thing to do.

The Proof That This Is Easy to Build

In case you’re picturing some massive engineering project, here’s the kicker: a developer named Rich Jones built a free, open-source version of this years ago called the Glance Bookmarklet. It’s a small chunk of plain JavaScript. It’s sitting on GitHub right now with over 1,600 people who liked it enough to “star” it and nearly 250 who copied the code to build their own version.

A single person built a working version of this in their spare time, years ago, for free. And it still works today as a browser bookmarklet that anyone can drag into their bookmarks bar and use on almost any webpage.

That’s the most damning part of this whole story. The thing you’d need to make your website more accessible to millions of people already exists, in working code, for free. It’s just sitting there, mostly undiscovered, because nobody decided to build it into the places people actually need it.

Why It Needs to Be Built In, Not Bolted On

Think about how other accessibility tools work. Screen readers come built into your phone. High-contrast mode is just sitting in your settings. Font size controls are everywhere. You don’t have to go find and install those things. They’re just there, baked into the device, ready the moment you need them.

This reading tool deserves the exact same treatment. Right now, the only way most people could use it is by going searching for it, finding a bookmarklet, and installing it themselves, which means the people who’d benefit most (the ones who don’t already know this kind of tool exists) are the least likely to ever find it. An accessibility tool that only tech-savvy people can find isn’t really accessible. It’s just a hobby for people who already know where to look.

The fix isn’t complicated. Phone makers and browser companies could add this as a built-in reading option, the same way they already added reading mode and zoom features. Website platforms like WordPress could ship it as a default option. And in the meantime, you, as a business owner, don’t have to wait for any of them. You can add a simple “Read Mode” button to your own site right now, using free, already-built code, and immediately make your business more usable for a huge chunk of people who are currently struggling silently or just leaving.

Want This on Your Website?

You don’t need to become an accessibility expert, hire a dev team, or wait around for the big platforms to catch up. The technology already exists, and it can be added to your site without a rebuild.

I build this kind of thing for business owners every day, websites, automation, and tools that actually move the needle instead of just sitting there looking nice.

Take a look at my work at sentientsprite.github.io/portfolio, and get in touch if you’d like a Read Mode plugin installed on your own site. No long contracts, no overcomplicated sales pitch. Just a simple way to make your website reachable for the millions of people currently struggling through it.

The technology isn’t the bottleneck here. It never was. The only thing standing between millions of struggling readers and an easier way to read your website is somebody actually deciding to flip the switch on.

Be the business that flips it.

title: The Traditional SEO Playbook Is Dead
snippet: Modern SEO Wizard Does your monthly SEO report say something like “we wrote 4 new blog posts this month”? If so, we need to talk. Because you’re probably getting ripped off. Not…
contentHtml:
Does your monthly SEO report say something like “we wrote 4 new blog posts this month”? If so, we need to talk.

Because you’re probably getting ripped off.

Not because your agency is full of crooks. Most of them aren’t. It’s because the whole reason blog posts used to be worth real money has disappeared. A lot of agencies just never updated their pitch to match.

Here’s what happened. Writing a blog post used to take a real person hours, sometimes days. That made it worth paying for. Today, AI can write a decent 1,200-word blog post in about thirty seconds, for next to nothing. The thing you’ve been paying thousands of dollars a month for is now something almost anyone can do for free.

So if your agency’s main job is still “writing more words for your website,” they’re charging you 2015 prices for a 2026 problem. Let’s talk about what actually matters now. It starts with the one thing Google cares about more than anything else: trust.

Why Google Cares So Much About “E-E-A-T” (And Why You Should Too)

You may have heard the term E-E-A-T thrown around. It stands for Experience, Expertise, Authority, and Trust. Sounds like corporate jargon, but stick with me, because this is the whole ballgame now.

Here’s the simple version: when something becomes cheap and easy to fake, people stop trusting it. Think about it like a flea market full of “Rolex” watches. Once everyone knows fakes are everywhere, the only watches worth anything are the ones you can prove are real.

That’s exactly what happened to written content. AI made it so cheap and easy to produce that Google can no longer tell a good answer from filler just by looking at the words on the page. So Google built a system to figure out who’s actually worth listening to and who’s just making noise.

That’s what E-E-A-T checks for. Break it down like this:

  • Experience — Did this actually happen to a real person or business? A plumber telling you what he found when he opened up a 1960s pipe is experience. AI can’t fake that, because it never opened the pipe.
  • Expertise — Does this person actually know the subject deeply, or are they just repeating what’s already online? Real expertise shows up in the small details only someone who’s done the work would know.
  • Authority — Do other trusted sources back this person or business up? This is basically Google asking around: does anyone respected vouch for this person? Backlinks and mentions from real publications are how that gets measured.
  • Trust — Is the information accurate and safe to act on? Is the business legit, with real reviews and a real track record?

Here’s the part that trips people up. You can’t fix E-E-A-T by sticking an “About the Author” box at the bottom of a blog post. Google’s own guidance for content creators says the focus now is on who made the content, how it was made (including whether AI was involved), and why it was made in the first place. None of that has anything to do with hitting a word count. A pile of generic blog posts, no matter how well they’re formatted, doesn’t prove any of it.

That’s the real reason the old playbook stopped working. It’s not just that AI writes content now. It’s that words alone don’t prove anything anymore. Trust does. And trust isn’t something a content mill can hand you.

Why Blog Posts Don’t Pull Their Weight Anymore

For years, the game was simple: write a blog post answering a common question, rank for it, get the click, turn that visitor into a customer. It worked because Google had no choice but to send people to a website to get an answer.

That game is breaking down for two reasons.

1. Google Is Now Answering the Question Itself

You’ve probably noticed those AI-generated answer boxes at the top of Google now. Google calls them AI Overviews. They read the top results and write you a direct answer, right there on the search page. No clicking required.

This is called a “zero-click search,” and it’s killing off a huge chunk of blog traffic. A 2026 analysis from research firm SparkToro, reported by Search Engine Land, found the share of Google searches that result in any click at all has dropped almost 23% in just two years. And when an AI Overview shows up on the page, click-through rates fall by nearly 60%.

  • That blog post about “how often should I clean my gutters” used to bring in steady visitors.
  • Now Google just answers that question on the spot. People read it, and never visit your site at all.
  • The simple, basic-question blog posts most agencies crank out every month are exactly the kind of content Google now answers itself.

You can still rank for those questions. It just doesn’t matter anymore, because nobody’s clicking through to see your page.

2. Anybody Can Write a Blog Post Now

The second problem is bigger. Decent writing used to be rare. It took skill and time, so there were only so many good blog posts competing for the same spot.

AI wiped that out. Now:

  • Your smallest competitor, with zero budget, can crank out a “good enough” blog post in seconds.
  • Google knows this, and it’s getting better at spotting generic, copy-paste-feeling content, then pushing it down in the rankings.
  • The only writing that’s still worth something is writing that comes from real experience or real data. Something AI literally cannot make up, because it never happened to AI.

If a blog post your agency wrote for you could’ve come straight out of ChatGPT, it’s worth ChatGPT money. Not agency money.

What Your SEO Agency Should Actually Be Doing

SEO isn’t dead. It just moved. The real value isn’t in writing more words anymore. It’s in the stuff happening behind the scenes. Here’s where a good agency should be spending your money instead.

Technical SEO & Site Speed

This is the foundation everything else sits on. If your site is slow, glitchy, or hard to use on a phone, none of your content matters.

  • Making the site load fast
  • Making sure it works well on phones, not just desktop computers
  • Cleaning up the behind-the-scenes code so Google can read your site easily

Schema Markup (Telling Google Exactly What You Are)

This sounds technical, but think of it as a cheat sheet you hand directly to Google. Instead of hoping Google figures out your business hours, prices, and services by reading your homepage, you just tell it directly, in a format computers understand.

  • It removes any guesswork about who you are and what you offer
  • Pages with FAQ-style schema get cited inside AI answer boxes roughly 2.7 times more often than pages without it, according to a 2025 industry study
  • Google has confirmed this kind of markup is part of how it powers its newer AI search features, as covered by Search Engine Land. It’s almost never something agencies selling blog packages bother to set up

Digital PR & Getting Real Backlinks

This means getting real, respected websites and publications to mention or link to you. It’s the closest thing to a stamp of approval Google understands.

  • Pages ranking #1 on Google tend to have roughly 3.8 times more backlinks than pages ranked 2 through 10, based on a large-scale Backlinko ranking study
  • An Ahrefs analysis of 75,000 brands found that being mentioned by name on other trusted websites correlates with showing up in AI Overviews about three times more strongly than traditional backlinks alone, according to a 2026 digital PR report
  • This is harder and takes more work than writing a blog post. That’s exactly why it’s worth more

Turning Visitors Into Customers (CRO)

Getting traffic to your site means nothing if nobody books or buys. This is about fixing what happens after someone lands on your page.

  • Roughly 68% of small businesses still operate with no defined plan for turning visitors into customers, according to a 2026 conversion-rate report. That means most of your competitors aren’t doing this either, which makes it an easy edge to grab
  • The same report notes that shaving just one second off your page load time can lift conversions by around 7%
  • Tracking actual sales, not just how many people looked at a page

Dominating Local Search

If you’re a local business or have multiple locations, this might be the single best place to spend your money.

  • Businesses with a fully filled-out Google Business Profile get about 70% more visits than those with an incomplete listing, and customers are roughly 2.7 times more likely to see a fully completed profile as trustworthy, according to 2026 local SEO research
  • Despite that, only around 35% of small businesses even have a claimed Google Business Profile in the first place, per a separate 2026 ranking-factor breakdown. That leaves an open lane for anyone who actually sets one up properly
  • That same research puts the typical return on local SEO spending at roughly $13 back for every $1 invested, one of the better returns in digital marketing

Notice what’s not on this list: a quota of blog posts every month. That’s on purpose.

How to Check If You’re Getting Ripped Off

You don’t need to be an SEO expert to figure this out. Just run these three quick checks on your current agency.

Step 1: Check the Invoice

Pull up your last few invoices. Ask yourself: how much of this money is going toward “writing content”?

  • If most of your fee is for writing, with little to nothing for the technical stuff, links, or conversion work, that’s a warning sign.
  • Ask your agency to break down exactly what you’re paying for, not just “hours worked.”

Step 2: Check the Reports

Look at your last three monthly reports. Ask: are they showing you actual sales and leads, or just “clicks” and “impressions”?

  • Clicks and impressions look impressive on a report, but they don’t pay your bills.
  • A good agency should be able to connect what they’re doing to real money coming in, or explain clearly why a number matters to your business.

Step 3: Check the Writing

Grab a few blog posts they’ve written for you. Run them through a free AI-detection tool online.

  • If it comes back as AI-written, you’re paying agency prices for something a free chatbot did.
  • That doesn’t mean AI-assisted writing is automatically bad. But if there’s no real human knowledge or experience added on top of it, you’re paying for something you could’ve gotten yourself for free.
  • One honest caveat: these detector tools aren’t perfectly reliable. A 2025 review of AI-detection studies found false-positive rates ranging from 15% to 45% across popular tools. That means some genuinely human-written content gets flagged too, so treat a “this is AI” result as a prompt to ask questions, not a courtroom verdict.

If your agency fails two or more of these checks, it’s time for a hard conversation or a new agency.

The Bottom Line

SEO used to be a contest over who could pump out the most words. That contest is over, and AI already won it for free. The real fight now is over who Google and AI trust more, who has the cleanest, fastest website, and who actually turns visitors into paying customers.

If your agency’s big pitch is still “we’ll write you blog posts every month,” they’re stuck selling you a strategy from a decade ago.

Go have the honest conversation. Ask your agency to show you their plan for site speed, structured data, real backlinks, and turning visitors into customers. If they can’t answer clearly, or blog writing is still the main thing they’re selling you, it’s time to find someone who’s actually focused on your bottom line, not your word count.

title: The Nature of Thoughts
snippet: the nature of thoughts Experts estimate that the average mind has between 60,000 and 80,000 thoughts every day. But what IS a thought? How can thoughts help or harm our lives? And…
contentHtml:
Experts estimate that the average mind has between 60,000 and 80,000 thoughts every day. But what IS a thought? How can thoughts help or harm our lives? And most importantly, can we control our thoughts and use that control to improve our lives?

Every human experiences the phenomena of thought daily throughout their entire lives. It may seem abstract or existential to even ask the question, “What is a Thought?”, but this is a thought in itself which humans have been having for as long as we can remember. Despite how easily you are already thinking about thinking, what thoughts are remains mysterious from a neuroscientific point of view. Scientific studies have shown that thoughts are a result of brain function, but which brain function? why do they appear? and under what circumstances? What makes a thought form? Neuroscience doesn’t have a clue about any of these questions we understand more about the nature of our thoughts than their origin or purpose.

Research consistently links negative thinking to an increased risk of mental health problems, physical health issues, relationship problems, and financial troubles. Your thoughts are a catalyst for self-perpetuating cycles. What you think directly influences how you feel and how you behave. So if you think you’re a failure, you’ll feel like a failure. Then, you’ll act like a failure, which reinforces your belief that you must be a failure. Someone who develops the belief that they are a failure will view each mistake as proof that they are what they believe. When they do succeed at something, they will chalk it up to luck.

All thoughts are repeated in the same cycle. The cycle begins with an Activating Event, the situation or experience that triggers negative feelings or thoughts. Then, our Beliefs are formed as we think in response to these activating events. Finally, we face the Consequences, the emotional results of these beliefs; these are also your feelings. You can see how this relates to both positive and negative thoughts. When you succeed and receive praise, you believe that you accomplished something. When you believe you are successful, you feel successful and thus repeat the cycle. Were you to fail, you would believe and feel like a failure, thus repeating another negative thought cycle.

More and more people every day are becoming less aware of the effects their thoughts have on their own lives and the lives of those around them. People often say they “can’t control their thoughts,” but if what we know about thought is true, this only reinforces the belief that you cannot control your thoughts. The first step towards gaining control of your thoughts is to become aware of this process. Become the observer, as if you were watching a movie about your life. Much of your life is spent doing rather than being, which means that you are on autopilot instead of being fully aware and participating in life.

References:

https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/consciousness-and-the-brain/201202/what-is-thought

https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/hope-relationships/201605/the-power-positive-self-talk

https://thebluesprogram.weebly.com/uploads/1/4/2/1/14217397/original_student_workbook.pdf

title: Quitting Smoking Using Hypnosis
snippet: Cigarettes and smoking have been a crucial staple in America’s cultural identity for over a century. Something deeply ingrained into our society cannot be easily defeated once it…
contentHtml:
Cigarettes and smoking have been a crucial staple in America’s cultural identity for over a century. Something deeply ingrained into our society cannot be easily defeated once it has taken hold of somebody. The chemical in cigarettes that makes them addictive, Nicotine, is known to be one of the most consistently addictive drugs ever created. Some have even said quitting cigarettes is more difficult than getting clean off of hard drugs. Not to mention many tobacco companies use alternative preservatives and additives to increase the addictive potency of their products. This makes Cigarettes and Nicotine the most widely used and accepted addictive drugs on the planet. Don’t be discouraged by this, and read on if you would like to learn about something anyone can use to overcome anything in your life, even something as addictive and controlling as smoking.

Smoking has plagued our society and I think any mother or teacher would agree it’s something we could all do without. The negative mental, emotional, and physical effects of cigarette smoking have always outweighed the short-term benefits, and today we are seeing this more clearly than ever. Here are some statistics determined by the Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC):

  • Overall mortality among both male and female smokers in the United States is about three times higher than that among people who never smoked.
  • Cigarette smoking causes about one of every five deaths in the United States each year.
  • Cigarette smoking is estimated to cause more than 480,000 deaths in the United States annually.
  • The major causes of excess mortality among smokers are diseases that are related to smoking, including cancer and respiratory and vascular disease.
  • Life expectancy for smokers is at least 10 years shorter than for nonsmokers.
  • Quitting smoking before the age of 40 reduces the risk of dying from smoking-related diseases by about 90%.
  • Tobacco use is the leading preventable cause of death in the United States.

-Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Smoking & Tobacco Use

How is Hypnosis therapeutic?

When we think about Hypnosis, we often imagine a man on stage convincing people to act like chickens or something absurd. When in actuality, Hypnosis is a common and widely practiced form of psychotherapy. The truth about hypnosis is that it is not a state of amnesia or a lack of awareness: hypnosis is a state of very heightened awareness and focus, similar to mediation.

Much of our reality is programmed by our perception and experience of different stimuli. The conscious brain is what reacts and acts during these experiences based on an image created by the subconscious. Hypnosis utilizes the deeply rooted power of your subconscious mind to analyze and contemplate why we are the way we are or do the things we do. By allowing a trusted Hypnotist to ask you questions about your unhealthy habits, they can assist you in re-training your brain to understand how habits like smoking negatively affect you. Once your subconscious understands all how smoking holds you back, your mind will naturally do whatever it takes to overcome the challenge of becoming healthier. This means that after years and years of subconsciously training your brain to believe you are addicted to smoking, using hypnosis can transform that belief. However, it’s important to keep in mind that hypnosis is not a treatment or cure for mental illness. People who have psychosis, suicidal depression, or who are on medications for psychological stability should be thinking of hypnosis as a supplemental device to help with symptoms that arise from these things.

American Health Magazine reported the following findings from a recent study comparing Hypnotherapy to Psychoanalysis and Behavior Therapy.

• Psychoanalysis: 38% recovery after 600 sessions

• Behavior Therapy: 72% recovery after 22 sessions

• Hypnotherapy: 93% recovery after 6 sessions

Regardless of your personal experience with smoking, a short Google search for “stop smoking hypnosis” will provide many places to research the science and effectiveness, different hypnotists in your area, and countless success stories that you could relate to one day.

title: Cymatics: the mathematic art of nature
snippet: Cymatics studies the relationship between sound waves and visible patterns in matter. It is an emerging field explored by artists, scientists, and musicians alike. cymatic pattern…
contentHtml:
Cymatics studies the relationship between sound waves and visible patterns in matter. It is an emerging field explored by artists, scientists, and musicians alike.

The History of Cymatics

The study of cymatics can be traced back to ancient Greece. Pythagoras, the famous mathematician and philosopher, discovered that the musical intervals created by plucking a string were related to the length of the string. He realized that there was a mathematical order in the way sound waves interact with matter.

In the modern era, cymatics was advanced in the 19th century by Ernst Chladni, a German physicist. Chladni used sand and metal plates to visualize the patterns created by sound waves. He discovered that the patterns created depended on the frequency of the sound wave, the shape of the object, and the material it was made of.

The Application of Cymatics

In the 21st century, cymatics has been embraced by artists, musicians, and healers alike. Sound therapy has been used for centuries to treat ailments. Cymatics takes it further by visualizing sound waves and their effects on matter. Practitioners can create a visual representation of the sound wave, which can help patients understand the therapy.

Cymatics has also been used in the field of music. A modern musical style has emerged with harmonious and balanced compositions by playing with the patterns created by sound waves. Musicians have also used cymatics to develop new instruments, such as the cymatic guitar and the cymatic drum.

Tanya Harris’s work with cymatics and architecture has opened up new avenues of exploration in architecture. By understanding the patterns created by sound waves, architects can create more harmonious and balanced spaces. Harris’s work with Hawksmoor’s architecture has shown how sound and geometry can create beautiful and functional spaces.

Conclusion

Cymatics is a fascinating field still in its early stages of development. Its applications are vast and varied, from healing to music to architecture. As we continue to explore the relationship between sound waves and matter, we will discover even more ways in which cymatics can be used to improve our lives. So, the next time you hear a beautiful piece of music or step into a beautiful space, remember that cymatics may have played a role in its creation.

title: The Mycelium Maestro: A Glimpse into the World of Paul Stamets
snippet: Paul Stamets, the “Mushroom Man”, is far more than just a mycologist. He’s an explorer of the fungal frontier, a visionary who sees in the intricate network of mycelium a vast and…
contentHtml:
Paul Stamets, the “Mushroom Man”, is far more than just a mycologist. He’s an explorer of the fungal frontier, a visionary who sees in the intricate network of mycelium a vast and untapped potential. His tireless work has revealed the secrets of these fascinating organisms, propelling them from the forest floor to the forefront of scientific inquiry and societal change.

Stamets’ passion for fungi began at a young age, blossoming into a lifelong commitment to understanding their intricate world. He delved into the depths of mycology, unraveling the mysteries of their growth, reproduction, and ecological significance. His discoveries have been groundbreaking, including the identification of new species, the development of groundbreaking cultivation techniques, and the exploration of the medicinal properties of mushrooms.

But Stamets’ vision extends far beyond the confines of conventional science. He sees mycelium as the “neurological network of nature,” a vast intelligence that connects and sustains the entire ecosystem. He believes that by understanding and harnessing the power of these fungal networks, we can solve some of humanity’s most pressing challenges.

His work has touched upon a diverse range of fields, including:

  • Environmental remediation: Mycelium’s natural ability to decompose pollutants and break down toxins holds immense promise for cleaning up contaminated sites and restoring ecological balance.
  • Medicine: Stamets has pioneered the research on the therapeutic potential of various medicinal mushrooms, paving the way for the development of new drugs and treatments for a range of diseases.
  • Agriculture: Mycelium-based technologies offer sustainable solutions for food production, including soil restoration, biopesticides, and even the development of meat alternatives.
  • Construction: The unique properties of mycelium, including its strength, fire resistance, and biodegradability, suggest its potential as a sustainable building material of the future.

However, Stamets’ impact transcends the realm of scientific applications. His captivating TED Talk, “6 Ways Mushrooms Can Save the World,” has inspired countless individuals to see the world through a new lens, recognizing the interconnectedness of nature and the importance of preserving its intricate balance.

Through his books, lectures, and tireless advocacy, Stamets has sparked a global movement of “mycophiles,” individuals passionate about fungi and their potential to revolutionize our world. He has shown us that the answers to many of our problems may lie not in technology, but in the very fabric of nature, waiting to be discovered by those willing to look beyond the surface.

Paul Stamets is a true visionary, a pioneer in the field of mycology, and a tireless advocate for the potential of these magical organisms. His work has not only revolutionized our understanding of the natural world but also ignited a hope for a future where humanity can live in harmony with nature, guided by the wisdom of the fungi.

title: The Schumann Resonance
snippet: Introduction The Schumann resonances are a spectrum of peaks in the extremely low frequency (ELF) portion of the Earth’s electromagnetic field (EMF) spectrum. Schumann resonances…
contentHtml:
Introduction

The Schumann resonances are a spectrum of peaks in the extremely low frequency (ELF) portion of the Earth’s electromagnetic field (EMF) spectrum. Schumann resonances are global electromagnetic resonances generated and excited by static discharges in the space between the Earth’s surface and the Ionosphere.

The Schumann resonance is an accurate measurement of the planetary electromagnetic field. This torus-like field of extremely low frequency (ELF) electromagnetic waves surrounds the earth’s immediate outer atmosphere. Schumann resonances occur because the space between the surface of the earth and the conductive ionosphere acts as a closed loop for various waveforms, so they bounce back and forth between the field barriers. Cosmic radiation is transported from the sun to the earth via ionized plasma in the solar wind. This energized plasma then affects the Earth’s magnetosphere and ionosphere, recorded by the Schumann resonance readings.

The resonant frequencies are between 3–60 Hz and have distinct peaks around the following extremely low frequencies (1),(2)

● 7.83 Hz (fundamental)

● 14.3 Hz

● 20.8 Hz

● 27.3 Hz

● 33.8 Hz

How to read the graph

The X-axis represents time, in hours, using Tomsk Summer Daylight Time (TLVA UTC+7). Use this world time converter to figure out your time zone and how the time converts.

The Y-axis represents the frequency between 0 and 40 Hz.

Date: A series of three dates are displayed horizontally at the top of the chart from left to right.

Time: For each day, a 0–24 hour sequence is displayed horizontally at the bottom of the chart.

The timezone is the location of the monitoring station, Tomsk Summer Daylight Time (TLVA).

The color indicates amplitude (strength/intensity). Black and blue are the background colors, and the scale moves from green up through red to the highest amplitude represented in white. (2)

Thesis: Does the Earth have an Aura?

Try to imagine a donut-shaped field around the Earth that, when stable, resonates in a constant and predictable cycle. When electromagnetic waves pass through this torus, there are surges and spikes in the measurable frequency. Since we cannot see electromagnetic energy, it must be measured and recorded to infer and predict future patterns. These electromagnetic waves commonly originate from solar flares and radiation, so we can make assumptions about what the Schumann will read based on how the energy wave will pass through Earth’s magnetic field. (3)

But this only scratches the surface regarding how important the Schumann resonance can be.

Another important thing to note is that the frequency is variable and not fixed. The graph goes through many patterns and cycles, and few are certain to be predictable. The more important question becomes, why would you want to predict the Schumann resonance?

The Schumann is also an excellent measure of something I will tentatively call “quantum certainty.” This is a measurement of how likely specific events experienced by the collective consciousness of earth are to occur, which means that the certainty of individual human experiences is variable and chaotic on a low-frequency day. Everyone has a unique day that is highly dissimilar from anyone else. In comparison, during surges of high electromagnetic energy, the events occurring in everyone’s lives will be very similar. This is crucial for us to consider and ponder as an empathic collective consciousness.

You can test and confirm this theory on any day when the energy is surging or by searching for a specific archived date and event. When you wake up in the morning, check in with yourself, then perform a double-blind test with a friend or family member by asking how they are and comparing it to your experience. Validate this confirmation by checking the Schumann resonance to see how the electromagnetics behave. Moreover, this can predict the future, especially when paying attention to the consequences and reactions of specific events.

What’s more, the frequency of Hz measured in the Schumann has been found to correlate to the frequency of our brains. The Schumann graph measures from 0–40hz, whereas our brains resonate similarly from ~.1–35+hz. We can note the effect that global electromagnetics has on our individual and collective consciousness.

Finally, to truly read and understand the Schumann resonance, one must observe and record as much personal experience as possible relating to the Schumann resonance. Nothing I’ve said here can equate to personal and direct experience with its energy. This is still a fringe science and deserves to be explored further by those qualified to do so.

title: Fentanyl and the Opioid Epidemic
snippet: Fentanyl. 2 mg. A lethal dose in most people.jpg — https://commons.wikimedia.org/ Fentanyl is a synthetic pharmaceutical drug that has gained unwelcome popularity in recent years.…
contentHtml:
Fentanyl is a synthetic pharmaceutical drug that has gained unwelcome popularity in recent years. Pharmaceutical fentanyl was developed in the 1960s for pain management in severe cancer patients; it was commonly used intravenously or through a patch on the skin. However, fentanyl is also being illegally synthesized and is sometimes added to heroin to increase its potency. Many users wrongly believe they are purchasing heroin but actually purchase fentanyl instead, which may result in physical harm, overdose, and death. Because fentanyl is 50 times more potent than street-level heroin and 100 times more potent than morphine, it may mean a high potential for addiction and abuse. (1)

How the opioid epidemic started

Although poppy flowers have been farmed for thousands of years by ancient civilizations and utilized for their medicinal benefits, it wasn’t until the 20th century that researchers discovered the potency of synthesizing opium from the poppy plant. Prescription opioids were developed in the early 1990s to treat acute and chronic pain, especially for cancer patients. In 1990, the first formulation of a fentanyl-based opioid pain medicine administered through a transdermal skin patch was approved for the general population. During the 1990s, pharmaceutical companies began aggressively marketing opioid drugs to the general public for pain relief. Five years later, the first formulation of oxycodone (known as Oxycontin™) was approved. In the early 2000s, reports of overdose and death from prescription opioids began to rise sharply, with OxyContin at the center of the problem. (2)

The prescription opioid epidemic

The first wave of the opioid epidemic meant a massive increase in people using OxyContin for non-medically prescribed purposes. Over three years, from 1999 to 2003, people using OxyContin without a prescription grew from 400,000 to 2.8 million. (3) From 1999 to 2019, nearly 500,000 people died from an overdose involving an opioid, whether it was prescribed or illicit. Another 130,000 people died from an overdose involving heroin, and the rate of overdose deaths involving synthetic opioids — including fentanyl and fentanyl analogs — increased by more than 16% from 2018 to 2019. (3) The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported over 100,000 Americans died of overdoses between May 2020 and April 2021, a 28% increase over the previous year. Drug overdoses now claim more adult lives than both car accidents and gun violence combined. (3)

How it became an epidemic

A single dose of an opioid can cause lasting physiological side effects. After 5–10 days of continuous use, the brain and body become dependent on the effects of the opioid. When heroin, oxycodone, or any other opiate travels through the bloodstream to the brain, the chemicals attach to specialized proteins on the surfaces of opiate-sensitive neurons (or brain cells). The relationship of these chemicals with the receptors has been shown to trigger the same dopamine response that rewards people with feelings of pleasure when they engage in activities that promote basic life functions, such as eating, exercise, or sex. (4) While opioids are prescribed therapeutically to relieve pain when these reward processes are activated in the absence of significant pain, the brain can begin to rely on the drug to produce ample amounts of dopamine to normalize its hormones. (4) Combine this easily-developed neurochemical addiction with loosely regulated prescription requirements and mass-produce the drug at an affordable price, and it’s no wonder there is an opioid epidemic in America.

Who it affects

I know two people who died, partially due to their use of fentanyl. One was a friend from high school who I hadn’t seen or heard from in years, though it appeared he was already on his descent into addiction the last time I saw him. The other person I knew had a much more personal relationship with the drug, and they were prescribed fentanyl by a doctor. In 2021, my grandmother was dying from stage-3 lung cancer, and we knew she didn’t have long left on this earth. The doctor prescribed her fentanyl for her pain as it was becoming difficult for her to get out of bed or swallow food. After her first dose, I noticed a difference in her behavior. She was definitely in less pain, but she was less self-aware, less conscious, and overall less herself. She only took fentanyl for six days before she passed away. Whether the user is a cancer patient or a recreational addict, the effect appears to be the same: this drug is a poison.

What can be done?

There are many services in place to support opioid users in both getting and staying clean. If you or someone you know is struggling with substance abuse, it is never too late to seek help. The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) has a national hotline and treatment referral routing service open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. SAMHSA’s National Drug Abuse Helpline can be reached by calling 1–800–662-HELP (4357). Narcotics Anonymous has also helped millions of Americans through the 12-step recovery program to live healthy lives of sobriety. Find an NA meeting near you. Ultimately, the opioid epidemic in America needs to be addressed with compassion instead of the exile and incarceration that legislation has shown past substance abusers. It’s time to follow the lead of countries like Mexico, Portugal, and the Netherlands: we need to decriminalize the recreational use of drugs while providing treatment centers and cracking down on the illegal production and distribution of these substances.

title: Understanding the Human Biofield
snippet: Our growing understanding of quantum physics and its place in the nature of reality has led science to validate the existence of the human energy field or biofield. The constantly…
contentHtml:
Our growing understanding of quantum physics and its place in the nature of reality has led science to validate the existence of the human energy field or biofield. The constantly developing model of our nature of reality has grown to acknowledge that the foundations of biology, built with the building blocks of conventional physics, must now adapt to include the growing foundation of quantum mechanics. These theories suggest living matter may not be constrained to the laws and limitations of conventional physics but may instead be interwoven with the laws of quantum physics. The evidence of the existence of the biofield creates the opportunity for significant progress in scientific understanding and for developing applications to industries like medicine, health, and healing.

The term biofield is described through Indo-Tibetan philosophical and medical systems as “a field of energy and information, both putative and subtle, that regulates the homeodynamic function of living organisms and may play a substantial role in understanding and guiding health processes.” Breaking this down, we can perceive a human biofield as a bubble of energy and information, meaning the biofield can be analyzed to learn about the subject. Furthermore, this energy appears to indicate the function and effect that a living organism’s biofield has on the reality around them, as well as their health and wellness. However, where science is just beginning to dip its toes into the concept that physical human beings also carry with their bodies of energy, the subconscious mind seems to have intuitively understood this for centuries.

Throughout human history, references have been made to the human energy field and how the environment, nutrition, exercise, emotional states, and various stages of life can affect it. In ancient eastern philosophies, we often hear about the chakras and aura that all humans possess. From the modern western perspective, we would simply call this the energy of vibes of people. The chakras are pools of energy flowing through the body following along the spine. They flow in a vertical column, drawing energy down and inwards from the universe, flowing down and outwards into our daily lives, up and inwards from the earth, and flowing up and outwards into our expression of the universe. This flow of energy creates an aura, which changes constantly depending on our state of being. How curious that these ancient descriptions of energies are so similar to what science is discovering about biofields.

Our understanding of biofield mechanics directly stems from the study of electromagnetic frequencies (EMF). Because our bio-electrical energy gives off frequencies and vibration, it can be reasonably assumed that the universal rule of “as above, so below” applies here as well. Our body is an incredible computational machine that is capable of interpreting, analyzing, and responding to incoming EMF stimuli, so, likely, we can also outwardly project EMF stimuli as well. While visible light waves only contribute to a small range of the electromagnetic spectrum, we know the many other ways that the human body and the biofield can be affected by the electromagnetic spectrum. We can hear radio waves from AM/FM radio and television; we can track and send information through infrared waves; we can see through the human body with X-rays.

Although no part of the biofield is visible, the biofield can be felt with the hands through pressure or temperature changes, or changes in emotional or physical behavior. The fascinating thing about biofield mechanics is the number of ways in which our biofield can relate to other forms of our biological and physical being. For example, consider the vibrations that you make using your mouth when you speak. Our brains understand what each other is saying because of the association with the vibration. Now consider when you begin speaking in a tone of anger or frustration, the vibration of your words changes so the listener can interpret your energy beyond the meaning of your words. When you begin shouting and waving your arms, your listening then is repelled by your energy. In this instance, we can see how biofields react to one another through verbal communication.

Taking this understanding of vibrations into account, we can expand our understanding of the relationships between biofield mechanics and other biological and physical phenomena. Consider, for example, the heartbeat, a measure of the frequency of pulses in which the heart pumps blood throughout the body to our vital organs. The heartbeat naturally quickens and becomes erratic when we undergo states of stress. Likewise, when we are relaxed, the heartbeat slows down, finding a balanced rhythm natural to our bodies. Because the heart produces measurable energy, it can be understood why the biofield reacts in unison with these behaviors.

We need to take a step back because a lot of conventional science requires seeing the proof and not believing the theory. Experiments were conducted to attempt to visually measure the nature of an aura or biofield in a plant. In these experiments, coronal discharge or the Kirlian photographic effect reveals a clear energy field in the morphological form of a living leaf even after being severed from the host plant. This suggests that patients’ subjective experience of a phantom limb after a limb has been amputated could be more legitimate than doctors and scientists thought. Because there is a persisting biofield that represents the amputated limb, the possibility of life and regeneration is possible, similar to how plants can be propagated.

Now, hopefully, in the near future, we can all see an Aura Photo Booth in our local mall or see an EMF page included in MRI analyses — believe me, I don’t think we’re far off. But I feel it may take a while for traditional sciences to catch up to and agree upon a collective understanding of the energy body or biofield. It is my hope that OTHERS may take interest enough to do their research, not by combing through the scientific literature, but by going out into reality, and observing, listening, and feeling your biofield, as well as the biofield of other living organisms around you.

Start small. Even a bee can perceive your intentions by reading your biofield. Pay attention to anything you interact with or that interacts with you. Notice how your biofield affects your reality. You may be amazed to find out how vital energy is to our bodies and the world around us.
